div.head: Further, the Book of the Prophets. and first, the Book of Isaiah. and in it there are thirty sections.

div.ab:
[First] the proem: Isaiah, the Jerusalemite prophet, was of the ¹⁵tribe of Judah and, in consequence of the marvelousness of his revelations, he was called the glorious. And in his time were prophesying Hosea and Amos and Jonah and Micah. He prophesied, moreover, twenty and four years in the days of Uzziah. And because he did not reprove him, prophecy was taken away from him twenty and eight years. But when Uzziah died, the Lord appeared to him, and he prophesied sixty and one years. Mar-Ephrem, however, in summing up the years of his ²⁰prophecy together with his silence, says that [he prophesied] one hundred thirteen years, that is to say, all the days of the four kings: Uzziah and Jotham and Ahaz and Hezekiah, in whose times he lived. Manasseh, however, killed him by putting him between two boards and sawing him asunder. Then he was buried on the bank of the waters of Shiloah. And some say that Amos, the prophet, is Amoz, the father
of Isaiah.

div.head: Section One.
div.ab:
(1:1) The ²⁵vision of Isaiah, son of Amoz, i.e., vision here is not specific, but generic, comprising the whole of his visions. It is different, however, from a revelation in that a vision takes place within the mind in sleep or in wakefulness [and a revelation (comes) through the organs of sense in time of wakefulness]. Isaiah, i.e., the salvation of the Lord. Which he saw concerning Judah and concerning Jerusalem, i.e., by the part he indicates the whole, for he prophesied concerning the captivity of the house of Reuben and Gad and ³⁰half of the tribe of Manasseh which (was accomplished) by Tiglathpileser; and concerning the captivity of the house of Judah which (was accomplished) by the Babylonians; and concerning the return and the rebuilding; and concerning the devastation of the house of Gog. (1:2) Hear, O heavens, and hearken, O earth, i.e., the inhabitants of the heavens and of the earth. And he calls the heavens and the earth to witness because they are present to all men of every kind and time. And by the mention of the two extremes he ³⁵includes whatever is between. Sons have I reared and brought up, i.e., with manna and quails. But they have
acted wickedly against me, i.e., they were arrogant toward me. (1:3) The ox knoweth
his owner and the ass the manger of his master, i.e., not alone the law of rational beings, but also the natural (law) of irrational beings commands to cleave to him who confers a benefit, but Israel was not guided by so much as one of these. (1:4) A sinful seed, corrupted sons, i.e., you have been intermingled with the tares of the gentiles and you have become corrupted. (1:6) From the ⁵sole of the foot as far as the brain there is not in her a spot which is sound, i.e., rulers and subjects together have become corrupt. Wounds and scars and affliction of swellings [<with å of b>], i.e., sins of many kinds. Not to be drawn together and not to be bound up, i.e., they have reached a point at which medical treatment is of no use for them. (1:7) And a desolation like an overthrow by foreigners, i.e., which has been left empty [by] the despoilers. (1:8) Like a booth in a vineyard and like a hut in a ¹⁰cucumber-field, i.e., after the fruits ceased, they were not inhabited. (1:9) If the Lord Sevå)ūth had not left to us a remnant, we should have become like Sodom and we should have become similar to Gomorrow, i.e., we, like they, should have perished entirely. (1:16) Wash and become clean and remove the evil of
your actions from before my eyes, i.e., with water, and with the spirit purge yourselves. (1:18) And if they be red as scarlet <with a of l and fricativeness of t>. (1:21) ¹⁵How has the faithful city become a harlot! i.e., she adhered to the idols who had not espoused her. (1:22) Thy tavern keepers mix water, i.e., thy teachers falsify their words. (1:23) And they hasten to return favors, i.e., only to those who give them bribes. (1:29) Fanes, i.e., places in which they used to hide and conceal the image of Ishtar, i.e., Aphrodite. (1:24) Woe, I will take vengeance on ²⁰those that hate me, i.e., in turn he encourages the people because also for their heathen persecutors (there will be) woe, when I take vengeance on them. (1:31) And their strength shall become tow, i.e., of wool in which no strength remains. And the two of them shall burn together, i.e., the wool and the tow. (2:4) And they shall beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into sickles, i.e., they of the house of Israel shall beat up their swords and shall make plowshares ²⁵of them because they rest from war. (2:9) And thou wilt not forsake them, i.e., even if they sin against thee, thou wilt not lose hold of them.

div.head: Section Two.
div.ab:
(2:13) The cedars (are) the young, the splendid; the oaks (are) the rich; (2:14) the mountains (are) the kings; the hills (are) the magnates; (2:15) the towers (are) the leaders of the armies; the walls (are) the horsemen; (2:16) the ships (are) the merchants; (and) the watchmen of lust (are) men on the lookout for lust(ful pleasure). (2:20) To worship, to nothingness and to the bats, i.e., ³⁰idols whom they were serving in secret. (3:6) And let this stumbling be under thy hand, i.e., hold out thy hand to us for we have stumbled. (3:8) The cloud to his glory, i.e., his goodness. (3:10) They greatly embittered the righteous one <with a of > i.e., from mᵉrårē (3:16) Stamping with their feet, i.e., they were dancing among the idols and entangling their feet with the feet of men; and provoking the Lord to anger. (3:17) The Lord will lay low the noble ladies of the daughters of Zion, i.e., the wives of the rulers. (3:22) And their armrings <with e of sh>. And their long gowns <with a of sh>, i.e., tunics which descended to the ankles. (3:23) And every ṣendå
of their adornment, i.e., the chest (?) of the bridal trousseau. (3:24) They shall bind on girdles, i.e., they shall
cover their nakedness with garments of wool. And bald patches instead of plaits, i.e., the hair that is removed. (4:1) And seven women shall lay hold of one man, i.e., because the men are becoming extinct by slaughter. And make our reproach pass away, i.e., when we have thy name, ⁵we shall not be charged with fornication. (4:4) And with a fiery spirit <with d>, i.e., with fervent zeal. (4:5) A cloud by day, i.e., the return from Babylon shall be like the exodus from Egypt. (5:1) I will praise my beloved, i.e., the prophet says: I will praise God, my beloved. The hymn which is due him from his vineyard, i.e., from his people. In the horn of the fertile place, i.e., in Zion. (5:2) And he enclosed it with a hedge, i.e., the law. And he ¹⁰planted cuttings in it, i.e., excellent men. And he built a tower in its midst, i.e., the temple. And he also made a winepress in it, i.e., the altar. And he looked for it to produce clusters of grapes, i.e., good deeds. But it produced wild grapes.

div.head: Section Three.
div.ab:
(5:10) For ten acres <feminine gender> shall make one ḥavīthå, i.e., a large jar. (5:14) On this account Sheol hath enlarged herself and opened wide her mouth without limit, i.e., that she may swallow down the wicked ones. (5:17) And the lambs shall feed on their just ¹⁵portion, i.e., the perfect (one). And the waste places which have been built up <with a of b>. (5:18) And like a cart-rope their sin <with å of ) and a of g and stopping of t>, i.e., the
more they draw (the more) it is drawn out. (5:24) The stubble, i.e., dry grass-stalks. And their root, their fathers; and their sprouts, their sons. (5:26) And he will lift up a sign to the nations from afar, i.e., he shall incite the remote nations to quarrel with Israel. And he shall whistle for them, i.e., his signal shall urge them on. (5:27) And ²⁰the straps of their sandals shall not be broken <feminine gender>. (6:1) In the year of the death of Uzziah, the king, I saw the Lord, i.e., (the gift of) prophecy had been taken away from him until then. And he saw him not with the eyes of the body, but through the emotions of the soul. Upon a high throne, i.e., above magistrates and rulers. And the hem <with e of sh> of his skirts filled the temple, i.e., the brightness which ²⁵radiated from him (was) upon those beneath him. (6:2) And seraphim were standing above him. Each of them had six wings, i.e., they were round about him, and it is not (a fact) that spiritual beings have physical wings, but their speed is symbolically represented to the prophet by the wings. And with two they covered their faces, i.e., that they might not gaze on him before whom Uzziah had dared to burn incense. And with two they covered their feet, i.e., ³⁰they were careful that there should not arise in them any thought regarding those below. (6:3) And they called one to another and said, i.e., there were two choirs, singing praises. Holy, holy, holy, i.e., a type of the trinity of the persons. The Lord, the mighty, a type of the unity of the nature (of God). (6:4) And the sills
of the doors shook at the voice of the one calling, i.e., a type of the destruction of the temple by the Babylonians and by the Romans after the crucifixion. And ³⁵the house was filled with smoke, i.e., a type of the anger of the Lord which waxed strong against them. (6:5) Because I am a man impure as to lips, i.e., I was favorable to Uzziah,
and I did not reprove him. (6:6) And in his hand a live coal, i.e., a type of the body of our Lord. He had taken from the altar with the tongs, i.e., a type of the priest by whose mediation the host is given. (6:13) And like the oak which has fallen from its acorn-cup (?), i.e., from its rootstock.

div.head: Section Four.
div.ab:
(7:4) Let not thy heart be shocked because of these two tail ends, charred sticks, i.e., ⁵because their kingship is near dissolution. (7:8-9) For the head of Aram, i.e., as the head of Aram, that is to say of Syria, is Damascus and her king is Rezin, and the head of Ephraim is
Samaria, and her king is Remaliah's son, likewise also you, Ahaz, are king of Judah, and the two of them shall not be able to overthrow you. And after sixty-five years Ephraim shall disintegrate from (being) a nation, i.e., he speaks concerning the ¹⁰[captivity] of Samaria by Shalmaneser, king of Babylon, which took place in the sixth year of Hezekiah. And he reckons from the year when the (gift of) prophecy was withheld from him, that is to say, twenty-eight (years) of Uzziah, and thirty-two of Jotham and Ahaz, and five full (years) of Hezekiah. But his word went into effect fifteen years after he prophesied. And some say that he reckoned from the time he prophesied, but because their guilt grew stronger ¹⁵God hastened their punishment, as (he also did) the deluge, before the completion of the term of the threat. (7:11) Ask for thee a sign, i.e., if thou art doubtful. Ask deeply or lift up above, i.e., seek the sign on the earth or in the heavens. (7:12) I will not ask, neither will I test the Lord my God, i.e., not so as not to test the Lord does he not ask, even though he humbly glorifies Him; but because he relies on Tiglathpileser he does not ask. And ²⁰on account of this the sign of the self-revelation of God is not given to him, but to those of the house of David and by this means to all peoples. (7:13) Listen, O house of David, is it so small a thing for you to weary man that you will weary even my God? Is it not enough for
you that you afflict me and do not believe my words, but also you would anger God as though he ²⁵were not able to help you? (7:14) Behold a virgin is about to conceive and bear a son! i.e., Divine Providence shall not depart from you until the Lord shall appear in the flesh from a virgin. And when you shall be offended at him, the kingdom and the priesthood shall cease from you. And the Jew says that he spoke of a young woman and not a virgin, that is to say, the wife of Ahaz would conceive and bear Hezekiah. Respecting him we say: Who called Hezekiah (7:14) ³⁰Immanuel; or whence will you show that before Hezekiah knew good and evil he rejected the evil to choose the good? (7:15) Butter and honey shall he eat, a type of this: that the youth, moreover, was to be great and strong in spirit. (7:18) And to flies he likens [the Egyptian], and to bees the Assyrian, for after they have afflicted them they perish. (7:20) The Lord will shave with a sharp razor <with vowellessness of w>, i.e., he will cleanse the land of the Assyrians, ³⁵great and small. Even his beard will he remove, i.e., their king himself. (8:1) Take to yourself
a large volume <with e of g and å of l>, i.e., a Κονταξ (shaft) of a scroll (or), a tome. (8:3) And I approached the prophetess and she conceived and bore a son, i.e., some understand this statement to be literal, that is to say, the prophet had conjugal intercourse with his wife. But our interpreters take it spiritually, that is to say, the power of ⁵him
who speaks through him settled down upon the Virgin and she conceived and gave birth. And the Lord said to me, Call his name: Hastening is he who takes captive and pressing is the spoiler, (8:4) for before the young child shall know how to call father and mother, he shall carry off the possessions of Damascus and the prey of Samaria into the presence of the king of Assyria, i.e., all these words have come true only in a spiritual sense concerning the gentiles who believed in our Lord. Otherwise: ¹⁰Where is Isaiah's son whom the prophetess, his wife, bore to him and who did those things? (8:6) Because this people have rejected the waters of Shīlōhå which move along quietly, i.e., the kingdom of the house of David which stands firm in our Lord without battle. (8:8) And the height of his wings (is) the full of the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel, i.e., the hosts of the Assyrian shall fill all the land of Judah. (8:11) It is like a grasping by the hand and he will turn me aside, i.e., he will guard them. ¹⁵Though they do not please him, he forgives those who will be corrected. (8:20) That they speak not according to his word, i.e., the evil spirits like the word of God, nor their priests who for a bribe speak like the prophets. (8:21) And he shall pass through her and shall be severe on her and (still) be hungry, i.e., the Assyrian will acquire the land of the ten tribes, and will not be satisfied.

div.head: Section Five.
div.ab:
(9:1) The land is agitated, i.e., she quakes before the Assyrian. (9:3) You have increased the people, but you have not enlarged the ²⁰gladness, i.e., the house of Judah said to the house of Israel who gathered together the Aramaeans for their aid. (9:4) You have broken as on the day of Midian, i.e., as Gideon massacred the Midianites. (9:6) And his authority is upon his shoulder, i.e., his cross. His name is called Wonder and Counsellor, God mighty for evermore, [i.e.], now every mouth of the Jews is shut, and that of all those [who speak ineptly of] the divinity of the Lord. (9:7) ²⁵And he shall support it, <with a of s>. (9:14) The tail (dūnbᵉthå) and in (some) codices [dᵉnuvᵉthå (tail), and in both of them with fricativeness of t.] (9:17) The Lord will not rejoice <with a of ḥ>. Wicked, <with ī of p>. (10:7) But he did not think thus, i.e., the Assyrian did not.... reckon that I, the Lord, had empowered him. (10:9) Belio, <with e of b>, i.e., the name of a place. (10:12) The strong heart, i.e., pride. (10:15) Lest the ax boast against him who hews with it, i.e., the Lord says to the Assyrian: I have
used thee as an ³⁰instrument for my anger. (10:17) And the light of Israel shall become a fire, i.e., against the Assyrian. And his holy ones a flame, i.e., his angels. (10:19) A young child shall write them, i.e., because their number has become few. (10:22) He has pruned and cut off, one (and the same) is the sense.

div.head: Section Six.
div.ab:
(10:24) And lifts his staff against you on the road to Egypt, i.e., Sennacherib intended to go to Egypt, and ³⁵since Jerusalem was on his way he beseiged it. But through the prayer
of Hezekiah he turned back in disgrace and was slain by his sons. (10:26) Like the slaughter of Midian at the mountain of Horeb, i.e., which was by the hand of Moses. (10:27) And the yoke shall be destroyed from before the heifer, <with vowellessness of sh>, i.e., the fat heifer. That is to say, the rule of the Assyrian shall cease from Judah. (10:28) And he deposits his luggage at Micmash, i.e., ⁵the Assyrian (deposits his) weapons of war. (10:29) Bēth bejåthån, i.e., a lodging for the night. (10:30) Whinney with thy voice O daughter of Geljam, i.e., the company that was on the point of going into exile. (10:32) Even today he halts at Nob, i.e., do not rejoice O towns of Judah because the Assyrian has departed from you, for there is yet evil in his mind. (11:1) And a shoot shall put forth from the stump of Jesse and a sprout shall spring up from
¹⁰his rootstock, i.e., literally, Hezekiah at present and, spiritually, the Messiah at the end. Now the stump is thicker than the branch, but the sprout is thinner than (the branch). (11:3) And he shall not judge according to the sight of his eyes, i.e., he searches out the insides of man. (11:4) He shall smite the land with the rod of his mouth, i.e., the land of the enemies with his curse. (11:6) And the leopard shall lie down with the kid <with e of n and stopping of b>. And these various beasts ¹⁵signify the various races of men joining together in the Holy Church. And a little child shall lead them <with e of n>, i.e., a simple, guileless shepherd. (11:8) And the infant shall sport with the basilisk <with vowellessness of t>. And the weaned child shall place his hand in the hole of the adder <with vowellessness of b>, i.e., in the burrow. (11:11) And the Lord will extend his hand again, i.e., as he delivered from Sennacherib so later he would deliver from Nebuchadnezzar. (11:15) And ²⁰he shall spread it out into seven valleys so that it can be crossed in sandals, i.e., the power of Egypt he likens to a river. (13:1) The burden of Babylon, i.e., he calls the revelation a journey, as something that carries with it the mind of the prophet from the place where he is to a spiritual and remote place. (13:2) Hoist upon the bare mountains a signal, i.e., the mountains of Elam and Media which are spread out (?). Lift up the voice to them, i.e., the ²⁵angels to the Persians that they should go to Babylon. (13:3) I have commanded the consecrated
one, i.e., the army of the Medes. (13:10) Neither will they give forth light... nor will he shine <with a of n>.

div.head: Section Seven.
div.ab:
(13:11) I will visit evil upon the world, i.e., upon Babylon which was ruling the world. (13:12) I will make men more precious than gold, i.e., the killing of an honorable man shall appear in their eyes greater than spoil of gold. Greek says, Those who remain will be more precious than gold, i.e., ³⁰the Babylonians are sought but not found because they have been entirely eliminated by slaughter. (13:13) By the rebuke of the Lord, the mighty, <with a of b>, i.e., because of the rebuke of his anger. (13:21) And their houses will be full of noises, i.e., of the beasts of the fields. (13:21) And the evil spirits shall dance there <with a of r>, i.e., they will rejoice in their desolation. (13:22) And sirens will sing antiphonally in their enclosures, i.e., a flying creature pleasing in voice which nests in waste places. But the Hebrew reads, starlings. ³⁵And jackals in the temples of their delight, i.e., herniqajåthå, banât ʾâwā.
And her days shall not be lengthened further, i.e., than from Ahaz to Darius, the Persian, who laid waste Babylon about two hundred years altogether. (14:8) Even the cypress, i.e., the
ʾabhūl tree which resembles the tamarisk. And the cedars of Lebanon rejoiced for us from the time you were laid low, i.e., the upright Israelites, as though to Belteshasar at ⁵whose death the kingdom of the Babylonians ceased, are speaking (this). (14:11) Under you maggots are spread <with e of k and r>. (14:13) Thou hast said in thy heart: I will ascend to heaven and set my throne above the stars of God, i.e., Satan speaks these (words) by the mouth of the Babylonian. (14:29) Let not all of you rejoice, O Philistia, i.e., because of the death of Sargon, your oppressor, for from his stock Sennacherib shall issue like a viper from a serpent. (14:31) And ¹⁰there is no one set apart at his feast days, i.e., assemblies like those on a feast day prepared for her destruction. (14:32) And... the angel of the nations is calling to Rabshakeh who was sent to Hezekiah.

div.head: Section Eight.
div.ab:
(15:2) And every beard is clipped, i.e., pulled out. (15:9) I will bring an addition upon Ribon, i.e., of chastisement. And I will think about those who have escaped from Moab, i.e., so that I may utterly destroy them. (16:3) Bring forward (your) opinion; and do profound meditation <with a of stopped g>, i.e., ¹⁵deep thinking. (16:6) His pomp and his pride and his ill-will, i.e., his anger. (16:7) Against the foundations of the walls, <with e of ʾ>, i.e., the towns.
(16:8) The vine of Sabmå <with a of s and vowellessness of stopped b>, i.e., the rich (one). The mighty men of the nations cut off her shoots <with a of g>, i.e., they lopped off. (16:12) That he is weary <with e of d>. He shall come to the house of the holy place to pray, i.e., to the shrine of his idols. (16:14) Within three years, as the years of a hireling, i.e., of Tiglathpileser who had been hired by ²⁰Ahaz to help him. (17:2) For the folds are forsaken <with e of r>. (17:3) And the remnant of Ephraim shall be as the glory of the children of Israel, i.e., it shall be brought low. The Hebrew says, And the remnant of Aram. And the Greek reads, thou art not better than the children of Israel and their glory. (17:4) And the fatness of his flesh shall be reduced, i.e., it shall be melted away. (17:5) Råphå'im, a place devoid of products. (17:9) Like a well which is silent, i.e., which, empty of water, yields no sound when a pebble is cast into it. (17:11) ²⁵And like the pain of men. The Hebrew says, Like an abounding (?) pain. (17:14) Behold the seizure, <with å of t>, i.e., seizure.

div.head: Section Nine.
div.ab:
(18:2) That sendeth pledges by sea, and with instruments of papyrus, i.e., the Damascene sends his sons as hostages with writings inscribed on paper made of papyrus, which is the Egyptian papyrus reed, to the Cushites to call them
to his assistance. (18:4) Be still and give heed to thy apparatus, i.e., ³⁰God says to the prophet: Still your voice and behold that which I have prepared. Like the fierce heat upon the river, i.e., strong. (18:5) And the bud is the children, and the blossoms are the young people, and the dry grass is the aged, and he will cut off the defective (zalilå) with the sickle, i.e., the reed (zalå), the rush. (18:6) And the birds of prey will collect about him <feminine gender>. (19:1) Behold the Lord riding upon fleet clouds and entering Egypt!, i.e., against the Assyrians who were planning to enter Egypt. (19:2) ³⁵And I will incite Egyptian against Egyptian, i.e., the king of Egypt against Tirhaka, king of the Cushites, and on account of this, when the Egyptian had overcome the Cushite, the Assyrian easily conquered him
and drove him from his place. (19:7) And the pond-weed upon the river, i.e., greenstuff, that is to say, duckweed which is upon the surface of the water. (19:11) Soan, i.e., the royal city of the Egyptians, which is Saʿīd (Thebes?). (19:13) And they led Egypt astray in the corners of her tribes, i.e., by the various idols which the different tribes set up in the corners. (19:14) The Lord hath mingled within her an erring spirit ⁵and it has led astray the Egyptian, i.e., while he was alive with an incurable disease he allows him to stray, as an intoxicated man strays in his own vomit <with å of w and ī of t; but some read with vowellessness of t and å of
l>. (19:15) And the Egyptian shall have no man to make head and tail, i.e., an organizer. (19:17) And every one who shall mention her <with a of n>. (19:18) There shall be five towns in the land of Egypt which speak the language of Canaan, i.e., the Palestinian Syriac. And one of them shall be named Heres, i.e., ¹⁰the same as ʿArīsh which is at the mouth of the valley which is between Palestine and Egypt. (19:19) And the altar that is to be erected in Egypt is not for sacrifices, he says, but for a house of prayer. (19:21) And they shall offer sacrifices and a meal offering, i.e., not the Jews, but the Egyptians according to their custom, but to the Lord, for they shall know him. (19:20) And he shall send them a savior and a judge and he shall deliver them, i.e., Josephus wrote that the high priest whose name was Hunjå (Onias) went to ¹⁵[Judea] and collected the Jews there and settled them in these five cities. (19:24) And Israel will be a third, i.e., a third in Egypt and a third in Babylon and a third those who remain in their own land. A blessing in the midst of the earth, i.e., through them the gentiles will be blessed and come to know God. (20:1) In the year that Tartan came to Ashdod, when Sargon, king of Assyria, sent him, i.e., Tartan was the commander-in-chief of Sargon ²⁰who preceded Sennacherib, and came (and) conquered Ashdod, the city of the Philistines. Then God showed Isaiah that the Egyptians and Cushites also should be led away captive. Thereupon he commanded him to loose from his loins the sackcloth which he had put on because of Uzziah and to walk naked and barefooted and to lament, because the dense of understanding trusted in seeing more than
hearing.

div.head: Section Ten.
div.ab:
(21:1) The desert, he calls Babylon, for like it, the Persians had made ²⁵her desolate and the sea (he calls) her king, because in subjection to her were many nations. [Like a whirlwind, i.e., you, the Babylonian who didst thus appear to us as an (21:2) oppressor and despoiler. Behold the Medes are coming up against you] (21:3) My loins are filled with quaking, i.e., the Babylonian speaks. (21:5) Prepare the [tables] i.e., eat and get ready for war. (21:7) He that rideth an ass, i.e., the Medes, for their horses, although small and slow like the asses, nevertheless are tireless and are nourished from the herbs of the earth and the leaves of the trees. And he that rideth a camel, i.e., the Elamites, who are expert in the riding of camels. (21:9) And ³⁰behold here comes a man from the horsemen, <with å of r and vowellessness of fricative k>. Without harvest and without threshing-floor, i.e., men harvested with the sword and took no time to heap up their corpses. (21:11) Dumah <with u of d>, is the city of the Edomites in Mount Seir. (21:12) Again you come, i.e., you return. (21:13) ʿåråbå <with å of ʿ [and] r [and] b>, i.e., the Arabians were descendants of Kedar, a son of Ishmael. And Saint Cyril ³⁵says that they are the Edomites, sons of Esau, who were called Edom, because the Greek joins this oracle to the one which precedes it. (21:14) With your bread meet the fugitives, i.e., he taunts the Edomites saying, You should have met your brothers with love when
he came up out of Egypt, and not wickedly as your king Balak did.
(21:17) And the archers... shall become few <with a of g and å of sh and e of t and n>. (22:1) Valley of Hezjūn (vision), i.e., the depression before Mount Zion round about Jerusalem. That every one of you have gone up to the housetop, i.e., to mutter incantations to the stars. (22:2) A mighty town, i.e., deriding her. Your slain were not killed by the sword, i.e., but they were ⁵the killed of God. (22:6) With horsemen <with å of r and vowellessness of k>. (22:8) The forest house, i.e., the one which Solomon built and in which he deposited the weapons. (22:15) Go to this sawkån, i.e., the name of the place of the treasury in the temple. To Shebna, the steward, i.e., this man was of the tribe of Levi and very intent upon the amassing (of money). (22:18) Like the distress of a ball in a land lax of hands <with a of w and fricativeness of t>, i.e., without ¹⁰rest but turning to all sides. And your glorious chariot will be the shame of your lord's house, i.e., because the shame of Hezekiah, your lord, you considered glory for yourself. (22:21) And I will gird him with your girdle <with å of i and a of h>. (22:25) And the tax which was put upon him shall come to naught <with e of sh>, i.e., the tribute.

div.head: Section Eleven.
div.ab:
(23:1) Tarshish, i.e., Tarsus, and
according to some, Karqidūnå, the metropolis of Africa Kåthīm, the land of the Greeks, ¹⁵and according to some, the islands of Elis (?). (23:8) And her Canaanites, i.e., her merchants. (23:15) They shall sing to Tyre the song of the harlot, i.e., after seventy years of captivity when she returns, like a singer she will collect men about her by her voice. (23:16) Play well, sing much, that you may be remembered, i.e., the harlot, when she becomes old, with her song makes men remember her youth. (23:18) Her [merchandise] and her wages shall be holy unto the Lord, i.e., ²⁰after the return she will pay her vows. (24:1) Behold, the Lord is about to destroy the land and tear it asunder, i.e., the land of the ten tribes by means of the Assyrian. [(24:4) The earth moans and sits in mourning... nay the height of the earth mourn <with e of (but) the Nestorian (has) a of >]. (24:7) The vines mourned <with a of l>. (24:9) Strong drink will be bitter to its drinkers <with e of n>. (24:10) Cellar <with a of m and å of stopped d>, i.e., where they sold wine. (24:16) I have a mystery, I have a mystery, i.e., God (thus) speaks because of those things which he is about to do
with Hezekiah. Woe to me, the evil doers have done unjustly, i.e., ²⁵the ten tribes who were carried captive to Assyria. (24:18) The sluice gates, i.e., the channels (of wrath) against the army of the Assyrians. (24:19) And the earth shall quake exceedingly, i.e., she shall reel to and fro. (24:20) Like a drunkard <with vowellessness of w>. (24:21) Upon the hosts of the height in the height, i.e., upon the Assyrians who exalted themselves with an angel who is from the height. (24:22) The captive of the pit, i.e., Hezekiah. (24:23) And the moon shall be put to shame and the sun shall be confounded, i.e., the objects of Assyrian worship. (25:1) ³⁰And trustworthy counsel, faithful from afar, i.e., in truth. (25:2) The sanctuary of the foreign ones, i.e., the temple of idols.

div.head: Section Twelve.
div.ab:
(25:7) Peoples he calls the tribes of Israel. (25:8) Death shall be swallowed up in victory forever, i.e., this (took place) literally through Sennacherib, and spiritually in regard to the death of sin through the Messiah. (25:11) And he shall spread forth his hands <with a of p>. The extending of his hands shall humble his might, i.e., spreading out. (26:9) ³⁵I myself have yearned [<with e of and t and a of w and b. The Nestorians: with e of and vowellessness of t and a of the second > for thee in the night. Also my
spirit within me advances toward thee. Greek: Out of the night my spirit has come before thee early, O God. According to thy judgments upon the earth the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness, [i.e., since thy judgments on the earth are righteous the inhabitants of the earth learn righteousness in accord with the righteousness of thy judgments.] Greek: Because light are thy commandments upon the earth. (26:10) And they shall not look upon the majesty of the Lord. Greek: The wicked shall so exalt himself that he can not see the glory of the Lord. (26:11) O Lord, they do not see the uplifting of thy hands. Greek: O Lord, thy arm is exalted, but they do not understand. They shall see--and be confounded-- the zeal of the people, i.e., thy enemies shall see the zeal of the people and be confounded. Greek: Zeal seizes the undisciplined. And like a furnace you shall consume them, i.e., the fire of your zeal, your enemies. Greek: Even now a fire consumes those who are opposed, i.e., according to the Greek the meaning of these words is clearer. (26:12) Lord, thou wilt preserve our peace, because according to all our work thou hast made preparation for us. Greek: O Lord, our God, give us peace for in everything thou hast made return to us. (26:14) The dead do not give life, nor do the great men raise up, i.e., those lords who were over us, (26:13) aside to thee, O Lord. Greek: The dead shall not see life, nor shall physicians raise up, i.e., the
gods of the gentiles are the dead who do not see life, and the sick who do not receive medical treatment]. (26:14) Thou hast visited them and made them contemptible, i.e., the tail instead of the head. (26:16) Lord, in distress they have approached thee, i.e., they have prayed to thee. (26:18) We were with child, we were in pain like those women who bring forth spirits, i.e., who think they are carrying spirits and not a child, and when they have brought forth, they are comforted. (26:19) Those who lie in the dust <with å of sh>. (26:20) Come, my people, enter into your inner rooms, i.e., endure
for a little while. (27:1) Leviathan, i.e., the Assyrian. The tortuous serpent, i.e., the Egyptian. (27:2) A vineyard of wine, sing to it!, i.e., sing a song to the remnant of the people who remain in Jerusalem. (27:4) I will shortly blow upon him <with stopping of b>. (27:6) He shall blossom <with a of n>. (27:9) Like rocks of lime that are reduced to powder, i.e., crumbled. (27:10) For the ⁵city by herself shall become desolate, i.e., Jerusalem, by Antiochus in the days of the Maccabees. (27:11) The women shall be broken who come to give her light, i.e., her allied cities. (27:12) The Lord shall thrash the grain of the river <with e of sh and b and stopping of t>, i.e., from the Euphrates to the Nile by means of the Assyrian.

div.head: Section Thirteen.
div.ab:
(28:1) Woe to the proud crown of the drunken (one), Ephraim <with vowellessness of w>, i.e., to the ten tribes who were taken captive to Assyria. (28:15) We
have made a covenant with death, i.e., ¹⁰with the Assyrian. (28:16) A choice stone in an honored corner, i.e., literally Hezekiah, but spiritually the Messiah. (28:20) For the garment is too short to cover him, i.e., he refers to the abolition and abrogation of the Mosaic law. And the warp is narrow and not full, i.e., it is insufficient. And some say that this indicates that the ancient law is not wholly abrogated, though it has become inadequate. (28:21) He will be wroth as the valley of Gibeon, i.e., ¹⁵as he was angered at your enemies in the days of Joshua, the son of Nun, (so now) he will be wroth with you. Strange are his works, i.e., after he gives life, he puts to death. (28:24) Does the plowman plow all day in order to sow?, i.e., he sows a little while, and for a long time it grows. So it is meet that my teaching of you should grow in you. Breaking up and levelling his land, i.e., digging to sow and then smoothing. (28:27) ²⁰For fennel is not thrashed by treading <with o of d>, i.e., moderately I am disciplining you because you are weak. (28:25) Spelt, i.e., millet, fennel. (28:26) He will winnow him with the judgment of God, i.e., when God moves the spirit (28:27) with the staff ... and... (with) the rods, that is to say, with the Assyrian and not with the threshing sledge that you may not perish entirely. (28:28) For not unto victory did we ever thrash him, i.e., we did not conquer the Assyrian with our army. ²⁵And with his hoofs they will crush him <with a of n>. (29:1) Woe, Ariel, Ariel, the town, i.e., the town of the
Moabites which David destroyed. (29:3) And I shall hem [you] in a cave <with a of m and g and stopping of t>. (29:9) You who are drunk... and you who reel <with vowellessness of r and å of ṭ>. (29:10) A sleeping spirit <with a of ṭ>.

div.head: Section Fourteen.
div.ab:
(29:22) Thus says the Lord, who redeemed Abraham, to the house of Jacob, i.e., the Lord who redeemed Abraham from those five kings ³⁰says to the house of Jacob. (30:6) The lion and the lion's whelp and... the adder and the basilisk, i.e., the kings and their sons and the chiefs of Judah who fled to Egypt. (30:11) And forsake... and turn aside <with vowellessness of p, imperatively>. (30:17) Like a signal upon the top of the mountains <with two r's>, i.e., Mar Ephrem explains it as a long stick on which a garment was tied and erected on a hill as a sign ³⁵which could be seen from afar. But the Greek reads snare instead of signal. (30:22) Dross, i.e., the useless (material). (30:24) Mixed hay <with vowellessness of b>, i.e., grain which has been tossed up by the winnowing-fork and cleaned.
(30:26) And the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun and... that of the sun (will be) seven-fold, i.e., a type of their increasing joy.

div.head: Section Fifteen.
div.ab:
(30:28) He cut off to the neck, i.e.,
the slaughter by the Assyrians will reach to the king. (32:1) Behold one ruling in righteousness, i.e., Hezekiah. (32:2) And he will be a man like a shelter from the wind, i.e., a ⁵refuge. (32:9) Wealthy women, i.e., the great cities that help Jerusalem. And daughters, those that were small. (32:19) And she will be brought low like a plain <with e of fricative k>. (33:4) Your spoil will be gathered <with e of n and a of z>.

div.head: Section Sixteen.
div.ab:
(33:7) And the messengers of peace will weep, i.e., the ambassadors who were sent to Sennacherib about peace and he would not hear. (33:9) And Sharon will be like a plain, i.e., a place thick with plants. (33:11) And you conceive thorns, and you give birth to stubble ¹⁰<with fricativeness of t>, i.e., straw. (33:14) And trembling has fallen on the pagan, i.e., on the Assyrians. And in some ancient codices fell is written in the masculine gender. (33:16) His food is given and his water is assured, i.e., this phrase is said to Solomon. (33:18) Where is the scribe?, i.e., as mocking the Assyrian. (33:19) His hearing is dull and his tongue stutters <with e of ṭ and c>. (34:1) The place of litigation, i.e., in which the Lord litigates with the Assyrian. (34:4) And all the hosts of the heavens will dissolve, i.e., the ¹⁵princes of the Assyrians, he compares with the stars. And the
heavens will be rolled up like a scroll, i.e., the kingdom of Assyria which like the heavens was exalted above the rest of the kingdoms. (34:5) For my sword will be sated in heaven, i.e., in that kingdom. (34:6) The sword of the Lord is filled <feminine gender>, with blood, i.e., of the Assyrians. (34:11) The pelican, the swan, the qafūfå, the owl; the crow, the great raven; (34:13) the ostrich, the camel bird. (34:14) And ²⁰the evil spirit will call to his companion, i.e., they will bewail the loss of their mates. There Lilith will repose <with e of l and ī of l>, i.e., an evil spirit which appears in the form of a weeping woman. (34:15) There the kite will gather <with å of j, like ḥa-jå-thå>, i.e., the djwg which is a vulture of the owl species (!). (34:16) Seek in the book of the Lord, i.e., in the book of the Torah. That not one of them errs, i.e., all the utterances of God were ²⁵fulfilled exactly. And they do not seek one another, i.e., the tribes of Israel did not select their lands, but the Lord assigned portions to them. (35:1) And [she will bud like] the autumn Kolchicum <with a of ḥ and o and å of l>, i.e., the meadow saffron which blooms early. (35:5) Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, i.e., the blind of heart. And the ears of the deaf will be opened, i.e., they will hear the Law. (35:6) Then the lame ³⁰will leap like the hart, i.e., he will run to learn righteousness. For waters have burst forth in the wilderness, i.e., Divine
Providence himself will refresh them. And literally understood of the time after the return, but spiritually of the time after the coming of the Lord.

div.head: Section Seventeen.
div.ab: This is recorded in the Book of Kings.

div.head: Section Eighteen.
div.ab:
This also is recorded, except the prayer of Hezekiah, (38:9) after he had been sick, and had recovered. (38:10) I said, I must go hence in the middle of my days, i.e., ³⁵my hope of life was cut off by this sickness which came upon me in my youth. Within the gate of Sheol I have left the rest of my years, i.e., I expected to die and surrender the rest of my days. (38:11) The pit, i.e., the grave. (38:12) My generation he has taken away and it has passed from me, i.e., my life has been taken away. Like the tents of shepherds, which are transferred from place to place. My life has been cut off like cords, <with e of r and in (some) ancient manuscripts å>,
i.e., the weft which the weaver cuts off. (38:14) And he chased away all my sleep, i.e., he caused me to get up from my bed of sickness. O Lord, by these they live, (i.e.), <with e of n> by (thy) mercies. (38:16) Behold I had great bitterness for my peace, i.e., after I had peace from Sennacherib, I had bitterness through sickness.

div.head: Section Nineteen.
div.ab:
(40:1) Comfort him, i.e., he bids the ⁵priests and scribes. (40:4) All their valleys will be filled <with a of m, but some have vowellessness>, i.e.,
their inhabited towns. (40:10) Behold his wage is with him and his work before him, i.e., the work of the payment of wage to the righteous. (40:12) The hollow of the hand, is when the fingers are curved, and the fist when they are closed. (40:14) With whom did he consult and (who) taught him <with e of ʾ>? (40:19) Pure silver, i.e., refined. (40:20) A piece of wood which is not rotten and fashions <with a of m> an idol which does not move, i.e., ¹⁰which does not move itself. (40:26) Who brings out their hosts by number, i.e., he determines the movements of the stars. (40:30) They will fall prostrate <with a of t>. (41:1) Be still, O islands, ... and let them renew <with a of ḥ>. (41:2) Who hath raised up righteousness from the east?, i.e., Cyrus, who brought back the captivity. (41:3) And he will not undertake the way on foot, i.e., he will not bring back the people on foot, but in chariots. (41:7) The carpenter encouraged the smith, i.e., ¹⁵to adore the work of their hands. He that strikes <with r> with the mallet, i.e., he who beats into thin plates. And he said of the joining it is good, i.e., the prophet mocks the idols.

div.head: Section Twenty.
div.ab:
(41:8) The seed of Abraham, my friend <with e of ḥ>. (41:14) Be not afraid, worm of Jacob, and insect of Israel <with ī of n>, i.e., the offsprings of the locust which could not yet fly. (41:15) Behold I will make thee like a new threshing-sledge, which shatters and crushes. ²⁰You shall shatter the mountains and crush, i.e., those of the house of Gog and Magog. (41:17) And their tongue is parched with thirst, i.e., as long as they were exiled. (41:19) I will put the cedar
and the boxwood in the wilderness, i.e., a type of their plenty when they return. (41:29) And their deeds are a wasted breath <with ī of n>, [i.e.] futile. (42:2) He will neither cry out nor clamor, i.e., he will not boast when he conquers Gog and Magog. (42:3) And a bruised [reed] he will not break nor will he put out a flickering lamp, i.e., he is meek and ²⁵lowly, literally of Zerubbabel, and spiritually of our Lord. (42:11) And Kedar will become meadows, i.e., Palestine, though it is dark as Kedar, will become resplendent with meadows, that is to say, Kedar will become meadows. The inhabitants of the crags will sing praises, i.e., the inhabitants of Zion. (42:14) I have kept still from of old, I shall keep still, I have endured like a woman giving birth, i.e., thy bowels are writhing; I will deliver them. (42:14) I will confound (and) bewilder <with a of ʾ>, i.e., those that ³⁰hate them. (42:19) Who is blind if not my servant and deaf like my messenger whom I send forth? i.e., my people whom I am bringing forth from Babylon and sending to its land. (42:22) And in the houses they concealed captives, i.e., the idols.

div.head: Section Twenty-one.
div.ab:
(43:3) I gave up Egypt on behalf of you, i.e., I destroyed the kingdom because of you. (43:14) For your sake I have sent to Babylon, i.e., for Cyrus who came
and freed you. (43:20) The beasts of the field will honor me, i.e., the foreign peoples ³⁵when they see my care of you. (43:27) Your forefather sinned, i.e., Jeroboam who made the calf. (44:5) And this one will write on his hand, The Lord's, i.e., although he be a foreigner, he will inscribe himself, The Lord's. (44:12) And he graves it with a chisel, i.e., with a chipping hammer which is small
like a bird's beak. (44:12) Even though he is hungry, [also] thirsty, i.e., the carpenter who constructed the idol. But the idol was unable either to feed him or to give him a drink. (44:13) And with glue he glued it <with e of t>, i.e., with gluten. (44:20) Their heart is fed with ashes, i.e., with the darkness of error.

div.head: Section Twenty-two.
div.ab:
(44:22) Return to me <with a of n>. (44:25) I will turn their knowledge to folly, <with fricativeness of k>, from ⁵saklūthå. (44:26) He establishes the word of his servant, i.e., Moses. And fulfils the mind of his messengers, i.e., his ambassadors, and they are prophets. (44:27) Who says to the deep, Be dry <with a of r, imperatively>. (44:28) Who says to Cyrus, My shepherd, i.e., my own shepherd, like My Elect and My Holy One. (45:1) Thus says the Lord to his anointed, Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped, i.e., not that he was consecrated like believing kings, but because he was an instrument to accomplish the ¹⁰purpose of God, he is called his anointed. And Cyrus was mentioned here
nearly seventy years before his birth, as also Agag and Josiah were mentioned before they were (born). (45:14) Tall men, i.e., mighty men. And in chains they shall come over, i.e., the Egyptians and the Cushites who are to be subjugated by Cyrus. (45:23) Every knee shall bow to me, i.e., a kneeling. (46:1) Bel has fallen down and Nebo is overturned, i.e., ¹⁵the statue(s) of Zeus and Hermes. And their idols, the graven images, were loads packed up, i.e., whose fastenings had broken and they had fallen down. (46:3) Who were [carried] in the womb, i.e., in Egypt, from which like new born babes they came forth. (46:11) I called a bird of prey from the east, i.e., the Persians. A man of my mind, i.e., Cyrus.

div.head: Section Twenty-three.
div.ab:
(47:1) O Virgin, daughter of Babylon, i.e., until now she had not been ravaged in war. (47:2) Take the mill, grind meal, i.e., ²⁰after your volumptuousness, you will become a maidservant. Clip your white hair, i.e., because your kingdom has become old. (47:8) I shall not abide in widowhood, neither shall I know the loss of children <with å of fricative k>, i.e., you will be deprived of your husband and children, even though your spirit be haughty. (47:10) It has led you astray <with a of l>. (47:11) Consternation <with a of t>. (48:1) And they have sprung from the stock of Judah <with i of m>, i.e., from the tribe, and the word is Hebrew.
But in the Greek minå (means) month. (48:11) ²⁵And I shall not yield my glory to another, i.e., to the idols. (48:13) And my right hand spread out the heavens <with e of ṭ>, i.e., stretched (them) out. (48:19) And the offspring of your loins like its pebbles, i.e., like the small pebbles of the sea. (49:1) He named me from my mother's womb, i.e., he speaks in the person of Zerubbabel.

div.head: Section Twenty-four.
div.ab:
(49:7) To the one whose soul is despised, i.e., to Zerubbabel, who, before the destruction of Gog and Magog, was held in contempt in the eyes of the people and of the servants of Cyrus. ³⁰Who is faithful <with a>. (49:12) And... from the sea of Senjam, i.e., the sea of Persia. (49:16) Behold I have inscribed you upon the palms of my hand, and your walls are ever before me, i.e., spiritually the type of the holy church. (49:21) An exile and distressed <with å of g>. (49:23) And they will lick the dust of your feet <with fricativeness of k after ḥ, and with its stopping before ḥ. The meaning is the same>. (50:1) [My] debt <with a of fricative b>. (50:2) My hand reaped the harvest and failed, i.e., my hand became tired
with their destruction. Behold by my rebuke I dry up the sea <with a of b>, i.e., a type of Babylon; and the streams are her hosts; and (50:3) the darkness is the heavens above her. (50:11) Walk
in the flame of your fire, i.e., continue in your tribulation. (51:1) Look to the mountain from which you were hewn, i.e., Abraham, and to the cistern from which you were dug, i.e., Sarah. (51:6) For the heavens will pass away like smoke, i.e., ⁵I will cause them to pass away whenever I desire, but my salvation for you will be for ever.

div.head: Section Twenty-five.
div.ab:
(51:9) Thou, thou art the one who didst cut a great gash, i.e., at the Sūf Sea, and killed the dragon [<in (some) ancient manuscripts betalti with b from abolish>], i.e., Pharaoh. (51:13) Where is the fury of the oppressor?, i.e., Sennacherib. (51:14) And his food will not be wanting, i.e., he who was staying away from Jerusalem. (51:17) The cup of terror <with å of ʿ>. (51:19) Those two things have happened to you <with a of m and e of l>, i.e., spoliation and famine. ¹⁰Desolation is incident to famine and ruin to spoliation. (51:20) Like the beet which is wilted, i.e., which the frost had blackened. (52:3) You were sold for nothing, and not with money you shall be redeemed, i.e., the Assyrian did not buy you for money that he might sell you for money. (52:4) My people went down to Egypt at the first, i.e., from famine, but I delivered them, and in like manner I will deliver them from the Assyrian. (52:11) Bearers of the vessels of the Lord, i.e., the priests. (52:13) Behold my servant is recognized, <with e
of fricative k>, i.e., he ¹⁵is known, and this was fulfilled in regard to our Lord. But he was called a servant metaphorically because he assumed the form of a servant and was esteemed less than the angels in his human nature. (52:14) Disfigured was his appearance from that of a man, i.e., by reason of the sufferings which he endured. And his stature from that of the sons of men <with vowellessness of the first l>. (52:15) And kings will shut their mouths at him, i.e., by reason of the wonders which they see from him. (53:1) Who hath ²⁰believed our report?, i.e., the prophet himself accusing the people, says: We have made our report of him, but they would not listen. (53:2) He came up as a babe before him, i.e., before the father, as Simeon bore him. He had neither appearance nor splendor, i.e., his deity was hidden in his humanity, and because of this we were disappointed in him, but He was beautiful in his appearance, more than human beings, as one said about David. (53:4) And we regarded him ²⁵possessed (of demons), i.e., when we saw him abolishing the law, and for this reason called him Beelzebub. (53:5) The chastisement of our peace was upon him, i.e., he took it upon himself to be chastised and to reconcile the heavenly beings to those of earth. (53:8) Who shall tell of his generation, for he was cut off from the land of the living, i.e., his eternity is beyond comprehension, for from the bosom of the father he went forth and came to the world. (53:9) The wicked
man gave his grave and with the ³⁰rich man his death, i.e., this statement is properly understood by inversion, and it seems that it was disarranged by the scribes. That is to say, the wicked one--Pilate--ordered his death and the rich man--Joseph, the counsellor--gave his grave. (53:10) Sin was laid on himself, i.e., he was condemned as a sinner. That he might see his posterity and lengthen his days, i.e., the seed of his instruction will yield fruit for ever. (53:11) ³⁵He is the servant of many, i.e., he subjected himself to all aspects of corporeal being except sin. (53:12) Because of this I will divide him among many, i.e., his gospel [will be] proclaimed
to the four quarters of the globe. And he will share the spoil with the strong, i.e., the first glory of Adam he would snatch away from Satan and return to his children as David has said, Thou hast ascended on high, Thou hast taken captivity captive etc. (53:12) And he was numbered with the lawless, i.e., with the two robbers. And he met with wrong-doers, i.e., the crucifiers. However, the Jews ⁵apply this verse to Daniel when his position was changed, while others (apply it) to Judas Maccabaeus.

div.head: Section Twenty-six.
div.ab:
(54:11) The one blown away, i.e., she was driven away by the whirlwind. Beryl, i.e., belūrå and bᵉrūlḥå are pearls. Capila, pīrwg; (54:12) ʾjaspåwn,
emerald; rock crystal, jasper that is the color of horn. (54:15) And all who turn from my hands will enter unto thee, i.e., the foreigners who take refuge in thee to escape my ¹⁰wrath. (55:1) [Woe, every one that is thirsty, come to the waters, i.e., O every one that is thirsty]. (55:2) Why do you pay money for that which is not for bread?, i.e., why do you waste for sacrifice to idols that are unable to give you bread? (55:13) Instead of the thorn, i.e., the kuba (thorn), the cypress will sprout up, i.e., the sweet-smelling silver fir. (56:2) And also keeps the Sabbath without profaning it, i.e., without violating it. (56:7) For my house will be called a house of prayer for all gentiles, i.e., a type of the election of the church of the gentiles. And (56:9) the beasts of the field, he calls the gentiles, and ¹⁵the beasts of the thicket, (he calls) the people of Jerusalem, whom he names (56:10) blind... and dogs, because they do not discern the wonders of the Lord and they are greedy. (56:12) And it shall be as today, i.e., we shall eat and drink and pass our day merrily.

div.head: Section Twenty-seven.
div.ab:
(57:6) Concerning these be comforted, <with a of b and l, imperatively, feminine gender; as masculine it has but one >, i.e., concerning the idols to whom thou didst pour out (libations) and made sacrificial offerings. (57:8) And behind the doors ²⁰upon the lintels thou
hast inscribed thy memorial, i.e., instead of the ten words which I commanded to be written on the doors, thou hast written behind them the names of the idols that you might memoralize them. Because thou hast uncovered to another than me and hast gone up, i.e., in captivity. And thou hast broadened thy bed, i.e., for defilement. (57:10) In the [guilt] of thy hands thou hast acted defiantly, i.e., through the deed of thy hands thou wast found guilty when thou didst scorn me. (57:14) Make smooth, make smooth, prepare the way, i.e., ²⁵for the return from Babylon. And lift up the stumbling-blocks from the way of my people, i.e., the idols. (57:16) For the spirit proceeds from my presence, i.e., I created the spirit of all who are alive. (57:17) And in her trouble she went in the way of her heart, i.e., because she loved the idols thou wast carried away to Babylon with them. (57:19) The speech of the lips was created, i.e., speech was created for praise of God and not blasphemy. (57:20) His waters cast up reptiles and mire, i.e., (the waters) of ³⁰the Assyrian, like (those) of the Egyptian formerly. (58:5) And he will bend his neck like a hook, i.e., a shepherd's crook, sawlagån. (58:6) The knots are the little sins, and the bundles, the great (sins). (58:11) He will make strong thy bones, i.e., he will strengthen. (59:4) And they have spoken emptiness <with i of r>, (i.e.), falsehood. (59:5) They have hatched the daughters of the basilisk, i.e., they have broken the eggs of a snake and brought forth the offsprings of basilisks. And they wove a spider's web, i.e., a net for the poor like that for the flies. ³⁵And he that breaketh it finds a viper <with a of
sh>, i.e., a snake like a worm, but every young from its eggs is a viper.

div.head: Section Twenty-eight.
div.ab:
(59:11) We roared, i.e., employed specifically for beasts of prey and likewise for doves. (59:14) For truth stumbled
in the open <masculine>. (59:16) And his righteousness supported him, i.e., when the Lord saw that they had no capable servants to help them, he saved them by his own righteousness. <And the eastern people soften the t's in all feminines, but we do not>. (60:4) And thy daughters will be brought up with cradles, i.e., upon the shoulders, but according to some, upon ⁵couches, while according to others, cradles is the plural of parūtå. (60:5) And thy heart will be enlarged <with u of r>. (60:6) The drove <with e of and a of fricative b and t> of camels will cover you, i.e., the caravan. (60:7) And... Neba'uth, that is to say, Nevīūth, the first-born of Ishmael. (60:8) Who are those that fly like clouds? i.e., those who return from Babylon. (61:1) The spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me and sent me forth, i.e., it is the son and ¹⁰the word of the father speaking these things by the mouth of the prophet. (61:3) The afflicting spirit <with a of m and k>. (61:5) Plowmen and vine-dressers <with å of k and vowellessness of r>.

div.head: Section Twenty-nine.
div.ab: (62:2) And thou wilt be called by a new name which the mouth of the Lord will bestow, i.e., the name of Christianity to Zion. (62:4) And thy land will be married, i.e., it will be endowed with abundance. (62:5) Thus will thy sons marry thee, i.e., the fathers who stand at thy head. (62:6) And his recorders will not be still <with a of m and stopping of k> before the Lord. The ¹⁵Greek: Those who remember the Lord. (62:10) And clear away its stones, i.e., from nᵉqålå. (63:1) Who is this that comes from Edom, with red garments from Būsår?, i.e., the cause of the redness of the garments was Būsår, [and literally it refers to him who delivered them] from the sword of the Edomites, and his garments were red from their blood, and spiritually, about our Lord who was questioned by the seraphim at the time of his ascent because of his crucifixion. And he answered them, I speak with righteousness and do much ²⁰to save. (63:3) And it splashed, i.e., sprinkled. (63:6) And I laid them low in my fury <with a of d>. (64:1) Hast thou not opened the heavens?, and come down. <Read with the even points>, i.e., thou hast opened. (Have not) the mountains quaked at thy presence? <Read with the lower point, interrogatively>, i.e., kings have trembled. (64:5) Behold thou wast angry and we sinned in them, i.e., this sentence is understood properly in the reverse order. That is to say, we sinned in them, in thy ways, and thou wast angry; <instead of d is written w>. ²⁵In the world we are saved, i.e., in this world. (64:6) And all our righteousness (is) like the cloth of a menstruous woman, i.e., out of thy goodness thou hast saved us, and not because of our deeds.

div.head: Section Thirty.
div.ab:
(65:1) I am sought by those who (formerly) did not ask me, i.e., by the foreign peoples whom I had brought upon the children of Israel. (65:3) Those who sacrifice in gardens, i.e., in the parks. And place perfumes upon stones, i.e., the piles of rocks. (65:4) And dwell in graves and lodge in caves, i.e., ³⁰because there the evil spirits revealed themselves to the magicians. (65:5) For I am to be consecrated, i.e., the consecration to demons was defilement and therein their rites were performed. (65:7) Double are they, i.e., against me are they. (65:8) As when a berry is found in the cluster, i.e., one unspoiled grape, a type of our Lord by whom the gentiles were blessed. (65:10) And Sharon will be a fold for flocks, i.e., a place that is dense with trees. ³⁵And the valley of Achor a cote <with å of b> for herds <with e of r>. (65:11) And you filled the tables for the gods of fortune, i.e., to the stars. (65:15) And you will leave your name as oaths for my chosen ones, i.e., they shall say: If we commit such and such things, it shall happen to us as it did to them. And the Lord thy God will put thee to death, i.e., in peace time. And he will call his servants by
another name, i.e., Christians. (65:17) For behold I create a new heaven and a new earth, i.e., the spiritual mode of life which the earthlings acquire through the Messiah. (65:20) And the infant of days will not be there any longer, i.e., the stupid person who does not understand. And he who sins being a hundred years old will be accursed, i.e., for a hundred years they shall abide after the return from Babylon, and then they would sin ⁵and be accursed by the sword of
the Macedonians, as the Book of the Maccabees shows. (65:22) For the days of my people will be as the days of the trees, i.e., of paradise. (65:25) The wolf and the lamb will pasture together, i.e., the vicious and the innocent after the advent of our Lord. And the lion, the kings, and the ox, the farmers, and the serpent, the destroyers. And some say that after the return from Babylon the men of the people will live peaceably ¹⁰with one another. (66:2-3) To whom shall I look and with whom shall I dwell, if not to the quiet and with the humble of spirit who tremble at my word. He who slaughters an ox is as he who kills a man, he who sacrifices a lamb as he who kills a dog, i.e., the sacrifices of praise are much more excellent. (66:5) Speak to your brothers who hate you and reject you because of my name, i.e., love as your brothers those who hate you. (66:7) And she shall bring forth a male child <with e of t>, i.e., ¹⁵she shall set (him) free <with a of t>. (66:13) Whom his mother consoles <with å of i>. So I will console you <with a of i>. (66:17) Those who sanctify themselves and purify themselves in the gardens, i.e., in the parks by means of magic. One after another in the midst, i.e., they are brazen, without shame. The end of the Book of Isaiah.
